messages.author: 89bc0322044bc587
messages.subject: mediating effect constrained to zero
parts:
Hi,

I've tested a structural model with indirect effects and used bootstrapping to check them, as explain in the tutorial. However, I was suggested that "the conventional way of showing the indirect effect was to compare a model with the hypothesized indirect effects with another model with the indirect effects constrained at zero". I am neither totally sure about the appropriateness of this method, nor how to do it in lavaan.

Any ideas about argumentation to not constraining indirect effects to zero or, if it is appropriate, on how to do it?

Thanks in advance,
Maria

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: mediating effect constrained to zero
parts: I was suggested that "the conventional way of showing the indirect effect was to compare a model with the hypothesized indirect effects with another model with the indirect effects constrained at zero". I am neither totally sure about the appropriateness of this method, nor how to do it in lavaan.

I've never heard that as a method for testing the significance of the indirect effect, nor do I see how it would be appropriate.  The indirect effect would be zero if you constrained either the X --> M path or the M --> Y path to zero (or both).  I've only heard about using model fit to test full mediation (i.e., constraining the X --> Y path to zero) or whether (in)direct effects are equal across groups.  But you can ask general SEM questions on SEMNET:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
